title: Complete relation quotient and descended differential maps
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n,s\geq0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, $R=D/I$, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak nR$. Write $M=\widehat\Omega_{D/F,\mathfrak n}$ with canonical derivation $\widehat{\mathrm d}_D$ [def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials]. Form the $R$-modules $T=M\otimes_D R$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $L=\sum_j R(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(f_j)\otimes1)\subseteq T$, and $N=T/L$, and let $q:T\to N$ be the quotient map. For $r\geq1$ put $R_r=R/\mathfrak m^r$, $C_r=\Omega_{R_r/F}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and let $p_r:M\to\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}$ be projection to the $r$th coordinate and $u_r:\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}\to C_r$ the map induced by $D/\mathfrak n^r\to R_r$. Then $N$ is a finitely generated $D$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and the elements $q(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(t_i)\otimes1)$ generate $N$ over $R$. The canonical map $\iota:N\to\varprojlim_{r\geq1}N/\mathfrak m^rN$, $z\mapsto(z\bmod\mathfrak m^rN)_r$, is an isomorphism of $R$-modules, and $\mathfrak n^rN=\mathfrak m^rN$ under restriction of scalars along $D\to R$. The formula $\delta(\bar h)=q(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(h)\otimes1)$, for $h\in D$, defines a well-defined $F$-derivation $\delta:R\to N$. For each $r\geq1$, the formula $\phi_r(q(m\otimes\bar a))=\bar a\,u_r(p_r(m))$, for $m\in M$ and $\bar a\in R$, defines a well-defined $R$-linear map $\phi_r:N\to C_r$. These maps satisfy $\phi_r\delta(x)=\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak m^r)$ for $x\in R$ and $\tau_r\phi_{r+1}=\phi_r$, where $\tau_r:C_{r+1}\to C_r$ is induced by $R_{r+1}\to R_r$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-formal-power-series-continuous-free], $M$ has $D$-basis $e_i=\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(t_i)$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. For $v=\sum_i b_i e_i$ and $a\in R$, tensor balancing gives $v\otimes a=\sum_i(\bar b_i a)(e_i\otimes1)$. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so the $e_i\otimes1$ generate $T$ over $R$, and their images $g_i=q(e_i\otimes1)$ generate $N$. Every coefficient in $R$ lifts to $D$ because $D\to R$ is surjective; the same finite list therefore generates $N$ as a $D$-module. This uses the scalar action specified in [def-weil-module-base-change] and the meaning of finite generation in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tags 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring) and 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), through the cited continuous-free lemma; elementary tensor and quotient calculation.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $F$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian] makes $D$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete] makes it $\mathfrak n$-adically complete. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] with ring $D$, ideal $\mathfrak n$, and the finite $D$-module $N$ from Step 1. It gives bijectivity of $z\mapsto(z\bmod\mathfrak n^rN)_r$. Under $D\to R$ the image of $\mathfrak n^r$ is $(\mathfrak nR)^r=\mathfrak m^r$: products and finite sums of images are images of products and finite sums. Each generator $az$ of $\mathfrak n^rN$ is therefore in $\mathfrak m^rN$, and conversely every coefficient in $\mathfrak m^r$ lifts to $\mathfrak n^r$, proving equality of these submodules. Hence the preceding canonical map is exactly $\iota$. It is $R$-linear coordinatewise, since multiplication by any element of $R$ can be computed using a lift in $D$; its inverse is $R$-linear by bijectivity. This proves the asserted $R$-module isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0306 (lemma-Noetherian-power-series) and 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3); application to the explicit finite quotient module.

proof.text: The coordinate derivation of [def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials] is additive, kills $F$, and satisfies Leibniz. Set $d_0(h)=q(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(h)\otimes1)$. Then $d_0(ab)=\bar a\,d_0(b)+\bar b\,d_0(a)$. If $h\in I$, write $h=\sum_j a_j f_j$. Since $\bar f_j=0$ and $q(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(f_j)\otimes1)=0$ by the definition of $L$, Leibniz gives $d_0(h)=\sum_j(\bar a_j d_0(f_j)+\bar f_j d_0(a_j))=0$. Therefore $d_0(h)$ depends only on $\bar h\in R$. Its descended map $\delta$ is additive, kills $F$, and satisfies the same Leibniz equation, so is an $F$-derivation with the stated formula. In particular $\delta(\bar t_i)=g_i$.

source.place: Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq), proof: Leibniz calculation for descent; the same calculation for the coordinatewise derivation.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq1$. The induced differential map $u_r$ exists by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]: the derivation on $R_r$ composed with $D/\mathfrak n^r\to R_r$ is an $F$-derivation. Put $\beta_r=u_rp_r:M\to C_r$. It is $D$-linear for the action through $D\to R_r$, and $I$ acts by zero on $C_r$. The assignment $(v,a)\mapsto a\beta_r(v)$ on $M\times R$ is additive in both variables and balanced, since $a\beta_r(bv)=a\bar b\beta_r(v)$. It therefore gives an $R$-linear map $\gamma_r:T\to C_r$ with $\gamma_r(v\otimes a)=a\beta_r(v)$. The coordinate definition of $\widehat{\mathrm d}_D$ gives $\beta_r(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(f_j))=\mathrm d(f_j\bmod(I+\mathfrak n^r))=\mathrm d0=0$. Thus $\gamma_r$ kills every generator of $L$, hence all of $L$, and descends uniquely through $q$ to $\phi_r:N\to C_r$. This proves well-definedness and precisely the required pure-tensor formula.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), equation-functorial-omega following it, and Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq), proof of the map from the tensor product.

proof.text: For $x\in R$ choose a lift $h\in D$. By Step 4 and the coordinate formula in [def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials], $\phi_r\delta(x)=u_rp_r(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(h))=\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak m^r)$. The map $\tau_r$ is obtained from the same universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] for $R_{r+1}\to R_r$; by construction it sends $\mathrm d(y)$ to $\mathrm d(y\bmod\mathfrak m^r)$. Consequently $\tau_r\phi_{r+1}(g_i)=\tau_r\mathrm d(\bar t_i\bmod\mathfrak m^{r+1})=\mathrm d(\bar t_i\bmod\mathfrak m^r)=\phi_r(g_i)$. Both composites are $R$-linear. Step 1 says the $g_i$ generate $N$, so their equality on these generators proves $\tau_r\phi_{r+1}=\phi_r$ on all of $N$.
